target_customer: Consumers selling used smartphones and electronics locally in San Francisco, with local buyers bidding in the app
problem: Selling used electronics on Craigslist meant spam, flaky buyers and haggling. FOBO guaranteed a price, paid sellers upfront and ran a 97 minute auction.
business_model: Marketplace with a guaranteed floor price, taking a spread by reselling unsold items it bought at the starting price

founders.name: Ryan Mickle
previous_startups: Yardsale (shut down to focus on FOBO)
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a product leader, user researcher and marketer.

founders.name: Ed McManus
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CTO on the YC page; no further background found.

competitors.name: Craigslist
competitors.what: Dominant local classifieds; Yardsale posted listings to it

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile app with auctions, payments and pricing from eBay averages; the harder part was operations of buying, grading and reselling unsold devices.

defensibility.rationale: Local resale apps were easy to copy and a guaranteed buyback required balance sheet; no data or network lock-in was shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it directly; Gone acquired FOBO and Yardsale Inc. in October 2015.

market_need_then: Used electronics had large resale volume and TechCrunch in January 2014 cited the pain of Craigslist spam and haggling; the beta sold 92 percent of listed items among 1,000 users.

branding.domain_note: Used fobo.net rather than fobo.com; fobo.net failed to resolve at fetch time.

identity.voice_and_tone: Speed and certainty pitch built around the 97 minute promise

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch, NBC News, Entrepreneur and Laughing Squid at the January 2014 launch.

brand_strength.rationale: Launch press and a memorable 97 minute hook, but a name with no stated meaning, a non-.com domain and later confusion with the unrelated fear of becoming obsolete acronym.

pivots.from: Yardsale, a local marketplace app reaching 130,000 users
pivots.to: FOBO, an auction app for used electronics with a guaranteed price
pivots.why: Founders shut Yardsale to focus on FOBO per TechCrunch 2015; deeper reason not sourced

outcome_analysis: FOBO came out of the Yardsale pivot, launched in San Francisco in January 2014 and reported a 1.6 million dollar raise, then claimed a one million dollar annual revenue run rate before Gone acquired it and Yardsale Inc. in October 2015 for undisclosed terms. The founders joined Gone's advisory board, so it looks like a small acquisition of a regional marketplace with limited defensibility.
notes: fobo.net did not resolve. The 1.6 million figure comes from TechCrunch January 2014; a cross-check outlet was not opened (the YC blog post of the same launch redirected and was not read), so treat as single press source. Round date is the report date, not the closing date. Aggregators claimed Yardsale raised 20K total and listed conflicting investors (Resolute, Gone); not used. Competitors are from the 2012 Yardsale coverage since the FOBO product launched in 2014; no 2011 dated competitor source found. Name origin not found.
